<issue>
[BUG] CloudFormation DeleteStack OOMs after persistent restart with ELBv2 resources
## Service

CloudFormation / ELBv2

## AWS API Action

`DeleteStack`

## Expected behavior

After restarting Floci with the same persistent storage directory, a
`CREATE_COMPLETE` stack containing an Application Load Balancer, target group,
and listener should delete successfully. Memory usage should remain bounded and
the Floci process should remain available.

## Actual behavior

After the persistent restart, `DescribeStacks` still reports
`CREATE_COMPLETE`. Calling `DeleteStack` then causes Floci's memory usage to
grow rapidly until the container is killed by its memory limit:

```text
sample_utc=2026-07-20T13:35:32Z mem=182.7MiB / 2GiB mem_pct=8.92% cpu=69.88%
sample_utc=2026-07-20T13:35:36Z mem=939.5MiB / 2GiB mem_pct=45.87% cpu=101.47%
sample_utc=2026-07-20T13:35:40Z mem=1.005GiB / 2GiB mem_pct=50.23% cpu=99.87%
status=exited exit=137 oom=true
```

The CLI eventually reports:

```text
Could not connect to the endpoint URL: "http://localhost:4570/"
```

Immediately before the OOM, Floci repeatedly logs loads of the persistent
ELBv2 state files, including `elbv2-load-balancers.json`,
`elbv2-target-groups.json`, `elbv2-listeners.json`, `elbv2-rules.json`, and
`elbv2-tags.json`.

## Reproduction

```bash
set -euo pipefail

IMAGE='floci/floci@sha256:0fb28cbebe2bb3a11e2b1336d8eaf2e9bf2feb411550b3ebe89ede88ae29965c'
DATA="$PWD/floci-persistent-data"
ENDPOINT='http://localhost:4570'

rm -rf "$DATA"
mkdir -p "$DATA"

cat > /tmp/floci-elbv2-stack.json <<'JSON'
{
  "AWSTemplateFormatVersion": "2010-09-09",
  "Resources": {
    "Vpc": {
      "Type": "AWS::EC2::VPC",
      "Properties": {"CidrBlock": "10.42.0.0/16"}
    },
    "SubnetA": {
      "Type": "AWS::EC2::Subnet",
      "Properties": {
        "VpcId": {"Ref": "Vpc"},
        "CidrBlock": "10.42.1.0/24",
        "AvailabilityZone": "us-east-2a"
      }
    },
    "SubnetB": {
      "Type": "AWS::EC2::Subnet",
      "Properties": {
        "VpcId": {"Ref": "Vpc"},
        "CidrBlock": "10.42.2.0/24",
        "AvailabilityZone": "us-east-2b"
      }
    },
    "SecurityGroup": {
      "Type": "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup",
      "Properties": {
        "GroupDescription": "generic repro",
        "VpcId": {"Ref": "Vpc"}
      }
    },
    "LoadBalancer": {
      "Type": "AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer",
      "Properties": {
        "Scheme": "internal",
        "Subnets": [{"Ref": "SubnetA"}, {"Ref": "SubnetB"}],
        "SecurityGroups": [{"Ref": "SecurityGroup"}]
      }
    },
    "TargetGroup": {
      "Type": "AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup",
      "Properties": {
        "VpcId": {"Ref": "Vpc"},
        "Port": 80,
        "Protocol": "HTTP",
        "TargetType": "ip"
      }
    },
    "Listener": {
      "Type": "AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener",
      "Properties": {
        "LoadBalancerArn": {"Ref": "LoadBalancer"},
        "Port": 80,
        "Protocol": "HTTP",
        "DefaultActions": [{
          "Type": "forward",
          "TargetGroupArn": {"Ref": "TargetGroup"}
        }]
      }
    }
  }
}
JSON

start_floci() {
  docker run -d --name floci-delete-repro --memory 2g -p 4570:4566 \
    -e FLOCI_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID=000000000000 \
    -e FLOCI_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2 \
    -e FLOCI_STORAGE_MODE=persistent \
    -e FLOCI_STORAGE_PERSISTENT_PATH=/app/data \
    -e FLOCI_STORAGE_HOST_PERSISTENT_PATH="$DATA" \
    -e FLOCI_TLS_ENABLED=false \
    -v "$DATA:/app/data" \
    "$IMAGE"

  until curl -sf "$ENDPOINT/_localstack/health" >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done
}

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=test
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=test
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-2
export AWS_PAGER=''

start_floci
aws --endpoint-url "$ENDPOINT" cloudformation create-stack \
  --stack-name generic-elbv2-persistent-delete \
  --template-body file:///tmp/floci-elbv2-stack.json
aws --endpoint-url "$ENDPOINT" cloudformation wait stack-create-complete \
  --stack-name generic-elbv2-persistent-delete

docker stop --time 30 floci-delete-repro
docker rm floci-delete-repro
start_floci

aws --endpoint-url "$ENDPOINT" cloudformation describe-stacks \
  --stack-name generic-elbv2-persistent-delete \
  --query 'Stacks[0].StackStatus' --output text
# CREATE_COMPLETE

aws --endpoint-url "$ENDPOINT" cloudformation delete-stack \
  --stack-name generic-elbv2-persistent-delete

docker inspect floci-delete-repro \
  --format 'status={{.State.Status}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}}'
# status=exited exit=137 oom=true
```

## Environment

- Floci version / image tag: `nightly-07202026`, `floci/floci:nightly`, digest `sha256:0fb28cbebe2bb3a11e2b1336d8eaf2e9bf2feb411550b3ebe89ede88ae29965c`
- Java SDK version (if applicable): N/A (AWS CLI reproduction; Floci reports Quarkus 3.36.3)
- How you're running Floci (Docker / native / `mvn quarkus:dev`): Docker on Amazon Linux 2023, persistent storage mode, 2 GiB container memory limit


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed, find the ELBv2 service code (e.g. ElbV2Service / repositories) and how it uses StorageBackend / StorageFactory for files elbv2-load-balancers.json, elbv2-listeners.json etc. Also find how CloudFormation DeleteStack deletes ELBv2 resources (CloudFormationResourceProvisioner). Report the relevant code (paths, line numbers, snippets) and anything that would cause repeated loading of storage (e.g. a persistent storage load() called in a loop or recursion, e.g. deleteLoadBalancer calling listeners that reload from disk, or infinite loop in delete). Don't change anything.

content.content: {"summary":"ELBv2 state lives in five StorageBackedMap-backed maps created once in @PostConstruct. CloudFormation DeleteStack makes one ElbV2Service delete call per resource in a single pass. I found no repeated load(), no recursion and no infinite loop. Each storage file is loaded once at startup, and deletes are per-key storage operations.","findings":["ElbV2Service.java:60-82 (@PostConstruct initializeStorage) builds loadBalancers, targetGroups, listeners, rules and tags via storageBacked(...) for elbv2-load-balancers.json, elbv2-target-groups.json, elbv2-listeners.json, elbv2-rules.json and elbv2-tags.json, then normalizes them and calls rebuildIndexes().","ElbV2Service.java:84-87: storageBacked() returns new StorageBackedMap<>(storageFactory.create(\"elbv2\", fileName, typeReference)). ElbV2Service never calls load() itself.","ElbV2Service.java:104-142 rebuildIndexes() iterates the in-memory maps once and calls healthChecker.startMonitoring/addTargets and dataPlane.startListener. It runs only at init and does not reload storage.","StorageFactory.java:57-100 create() reuses an existing backend per file path (backendsByPath) and calls inner.load() only when it creates a new backend. loadAll() (StorageFactory.java:106-108) has a single call site, EmulatorLifecycle.java:168.","PersistentStorage.java:83-97 and WalStorage.java:124-135 load() read the whole file into the store. These are the only disk reads, and nothing on the ELBv2 delete path calls them.","StorageBackedMap.java:42-48 get() and :78-86 remove() read or delete a single key through storage. entrySet iteration (:95-150) snapshots keys. None of these trigger a file reload.","ElbV2Service.java:223-247 deleteLoadBalancer removes the LB, then cascades once over lbToListeners (dataPlane.stopListener, regionListeners.remove, rule removal), clears tgToLbs and tags, and calls loadBalancers.put(region, regionLbs). It does not call deleteListener, so there is no recursion.","ElbV2Service.java:385-395 deleteTargetGroup throws ResourceInUse if tgToLbs is non-empty, otherwise removes the TG and persists. ElbV2Service.java:515-535 deleteListener returns early if the listener is already gone, otherwise calls unlinkUnreferencedTargetGroups. ElbV2Service.java:655-670 deleteRule is similar.","ElbV2Service.java:~1083-1110 unlinkUnreferencedTargetGroups iterates listeners, rules and tgToLbs once each with no recursion, calling removeLoadBalancerReference for each unreferenced TG.","CloudFormationResourceProvisioner.java:385-421 delete(StackResource) dispatches custom resources and otherwise calls delete(type, physicalId, region). Lines 451-454 map AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::{LoadBalancer,TargetGroup,Listener,ListenerRule} to elbV2Service.deleteLoadBalancer/deleteTargetGroup/deleteListener/deleteRule, each called once per resource.","CloudFormationService.java:~623-665 deleteStackResources copies the resources, reverses them, and makes one provisioner.delete() attempt per resource. Failures are marked DELETE_FAILED and the loop continues. There is no retry loop. A later CFN Listener delete after the LB cascade is a no-op because deleteListener returns early.","Conclusion: no infinite loop or repeated load exists in the ELBv2 delete path. The only repetition is the CFN DELETE_FAILED re-attempt, which happens only when the user retries DeleteStack. deleteLoadBalancer and deleteListener do whole-region put() writes (ElbV2Service.java:~245, ~530), which is write amplification, not reloading."],"confidence":0.8}

input.instruction: In /testbed, look at StorageFactory.create (src/main/java/.../core/storage/StorageFactory.java) and its callers; look at scope annotations of ElbV2Service (and anything else) and how CloudFormationResourceProvisioner/CloudFormationService get ElbV2Service (Instance<>, new, Provider?). Also check whether ElbV2Service has circular dependency with something (healthChecker, dataPlane) that is dependent-scoped / re-instantiated. Also check what log message prints 'Loaded ... elbv2-load-balancers.json' and why it could repeat during DeleteStack. Report findings with snippets; change nothing.

content.content: {"summary":"StorageFactory is ApplicationScoped and dedupes backends by file path, so a repeat create() for the same elbv2 file reuses the backend without reloading it. ElbV2Service is ApplicationScoped and loads its elbv2-*.json stores once in @PostConstruct. The 'Loaded N entries from …elbv2-load-balancers.json' line comes from load(), which runs at boot via loadAll() or on first create(). I found no code path in DeleteStack that reloads elbv2 storage, so a repeat most likely means a second boot-time loadAll() or another load() call. I did not confirm that from logs. Nothing was modified.","findings":["StorageFactory.java:24 is @ApplicationScoped. create() at :57 is synchronized and reuses backends keyed by path in backendsByPath (:34, :67-73). A repeat call for the same file returns the existing backend and logs only a debug 'Reusing existing...' message, with no load().","StorageFactory.java:96 calls inner.load() only when a new backend is created. loadAll() (:106-110) calls load() on every backend and is invoked only from EmulatorLifecycle.java:168 during boot.","ElbV2Service.java:23 is @ApplicationScoped. Dependencies are field-injected with @Inject: dataPlane (:26-27), healthChecker (:29-30), regionResolver, ec2Service, storageFactory (:32-41), config. Production code uses no Instance, Provider, or new. `new ElbV2Service()` appears only in tests (ElbV2ServiceTest.java:66, :262).","ElbV2Service.java:60-78 (@PostConstruct initializeStorage) calls storageBacked() for elbv2-load-balancers.json, elbv2-target-groups.json, elbv2-listeners.json, elbv2-rules.json and elbv2-tags.json. storageBacked() at :85-87 calls storageFactory.create(\"elbv2\", fileName, ...). It returns early if storageFactory is null (:62-63).","CloudFormationResourceProvisioner.java:105 is @ApplicationScoped and receives ElbV2Service through its @Inject constructor (:165-182, field :149). This is direct injection, not Instance or Provider. Delete paths call elbV2Service.deleteLoadBalancer and related methods at :451-454.","CloudFormationService.java:42 is @ApplicationScoped and takes CloudFormationResourceProvisioner through its @Inject constructor (:69-70). DeleteStack runs asynchronously via executor.submit (:298-314) and reaches the provisioner's delete logic. I found no ElbV2Service reload on that path.","Circular reference: ElbV2Service has field injection of ElbV2DataPlane (:27) and ElbV2HealthChecker (:30). ElbV2DataPlane.java:42 is @ApplicationScoped and injects ElbV2Service back (:55). Both sides are ApplicationScoped client proxies, so the cycle resolves without re-instantiation. ElbV2HealthChecker.java:22 is @ApplicationScoped; its @Inject constructor (:36-37) takes Vertx, EmulatorConfig and Ec2Service, with no back-reference to ElbV2Service.","The log text comes from PersistentStorage.java:92 (`LOG.infov(\"Loaded {0} entries from {1}\", store.size(), filePath)`) or from HybridStorage.java:103 with the same text. Which one fires depends on the resolved storage mode for 'elbv2' (ServiceConfigAccess.storageMode, falling back to config.storage().mode()). WalStorage.java:130 logs a different snapshot message."],"confidence":0.6}
